reel.caption:
Got more than ₹50,000 in gifts this year? Do you owe tax?

Gifts from non-relatives become taxable income once they cross ₹50,000 in total in a tax year. The rule continues under the new Income-tax Act.
Gifts from close relatives (parents, spouse, siblings, children, grandparents) are tax-free at any amount, and so are gifts at your wedding.
The limit counts all your gifts from friends and colleagues across the year, not each one.

Sources: a tax explainer under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Aug 2026) and two business news explainers on festive gift tax.
